002_p: Five countries, five neighborhoods, one question — what stirs when young people are given room to practice community life where they already live?
016_alt: Young people sitting together outdoors, laughing, with folded paper shapes around them
017_figcaption: Photo by Hannah Busing on Unsplash. Photos from the five neighborhood teams to come.
019_p: Across urban and rural Asia, young people are experiencing rising loneliness and disconnection from community life. But something else is also true: many of them sense that more is possible. They are not indifferent. They are waiting for conditions in which their own capacity might become useful — to others, and to themselves.
020_p: The Asia Exchange creates those conditions, across five countries and one shared question: what begins to stir, inwardly and outwardly, when young people are given space to practice coherent community life in their own neighborhoods?
021_div: A journey of self-discovery and neighborhood rediscovery
024_p: begin not with a project plan but with honest self-examination — the assumptions and prejudices that keep neighbors strangers, and the capacity to see what is already alive nearby but unnamed. Through a series of Global Labs they move along one continuous inner-outer arc: first going beneath the surface and practicing conversations that go deeper than usual; then imagining, not from what is missing but from what is quietly already present; then planning and acting, designing a neighborhood activation together with neighbors and local organizations.
026_p: An Orientation Lab opens the year, then three Global Labs, each on a two-month Action and Reflection cycle, bringing practitioners from all five countries into one room. Each lab meets one root condition as a reality to encounter in the neighborhood, not a topic to study.
030_p: The five country teams meet each other, the shared root system, and what the year asks of a BridgeBuilder.
034_p: Hero to Protagonist. Going beneath the surface of how neighbors see each other.
039_p: Beginning from what is already alive, and imagining what youth could activate.
044_p: From learning to leading: each team plans its own Pop-Up Lab.
051_p: Each journey culminates in a lab that is not an event but an invitation — co-created with neighbors and taking its own local form.
052_b: One lab meets in person, hosted by a local team and open to its neighbors.
054_p: Multicultural dialogue across cultural and linguistic difference.
058_p: ME=WE dialogue and meaningful conversation spaces.
060_p: Storytelling, digital mapping, and intergenerational wisdom circles.
062_p: Junior-youth animator networks as everyday neighborhood presence.
066_p: Practitioners from all five countries travel to each other’s neighborhoods — walking the streets, co-facilitating, witnessing what has grown, carrying it home. This is not five parallel projects. It is one network, strengthening what each team already wants to do.
067_p: A prototype, not an event. The one-year frame is not the container.
071_h2: Bring the Exchange to your own neighborhood.
